Patient.template: Using only the retrieved PostgreSQL schema metadata, find the relation or joins that represent a patient in any of these source schemas: {source_schemas}. Generate one SELECT filtered to patient key {patient_key}. Return exactly one row and these aliases: patient key AS _patient_key, administrative gender AS _gender, death date/time AS _death_datetime. Use NULL only for unavailable optional values. Do not assume any table or column name. Fully qualify every relation.

Encounter.template: Using only the retrieved PostgreSQL schema metadata, select the broadest single patient-level relation that represents complete hospital encounters, admissions, or visits in any of these source schemas: {source_schemas}. The selected relation itself MUST document a non-null patient key, encounter/visit key, encounter/admission type, start date/time, and end date/time; do not join a narrower stay, transfer, or episode relation to construct or fill these values. Return every matching encounter for patient key {patient_key}{encounter_override_clause}, up to limit {limit}. Do not select an ICU-stay-only, unit-transfer-only, emergency-department-only, or other narrower subset relation when a broader patient encounter/admission relation is documented. Select the documented encounter/visit key column directly AS _encounter_key; never concatenate it with a stay, transfer, or episode key. Select the documented encounter/admission type column directly AS _encounter_type; a CASE expression, COALESCE fallback, or quoted type label is forbidden. Do not use DISTINCT, grouping, window filtering, or a join that can remove or multiply encounter rows. Return: patient key AS _patient_key, encounter/visit key AS _encounter_key, documented source encounter/admission type AS _encounter_type, start date/time AS _start_datetime, end date/time AS _end_datetime. Every output expression MUST be a documented source column or NULL. A quoted label such as 'Encounter', 'Admission', or 'ICU Stay' is forbidden. Order by start date/time deterministically and place the final LIMIT {limit} after ORDER BY. Do not assume any table or column name. Fully qualify every relation.

Condition.template: Using only the retrieved PostgreSQL schema metadata, select the broadest single clinical event relation for diagnoses or conditions in any of these source schemas: {source_schemas}, plus at most one matching dictionary relation when its join columns are documented. Do not combine procedures, billing events, or multiple condition sources. Generate a SELECT filtered only to patient key {patient_key} and all encounter keys in ({encounter_keys}); do not select only one encounter. Preserve every matching condition row from the selected event relation. Any optional dictionary join MUST be a LEFT JOIN using every column of the documented dictionary composite key so that it cannot remove or multiply event rows; an INNER JOIN or a partial-key join is forbidden. If the complete dictionary join key cannot be proven from metadata, do not join and return NULL AS _display. Return: patient key AS _patient_key, encounter key AS _encounter_key, a non-null unique stable condition-row key built from documented columns AS _resource_key, code AS _code, canonical code-system URI AS _code_system only when stored in a source column otherwise NULL, source description from an actually joined documented dictionary column AS _display otherwise NULL. Prefer a documented event-row primary key or its complete documented composite key. Never use LIMIT per encounter; apply only the final total limit {limit}. Every expression must use documented columns or NULL. Never invent values, descriptions, systems, or placeholder text. Order deterministically and limit {limit}. Fully qualify every relation.

Procedure.template: Using only the retrieved PostgreSQL schema metadata, select the broadest hospital encounter-level relation for coded patient procedures in any of these source schemas: {source_schemas}, plus at most one matching procedure-code dictionary relation when documented. A diagnoses or conditions dictionary is not a procedure dictionary and MUST NOT be joined. When a candidate relation documents both a procedure code and its code version, prefer it over relations that contain only billing, charge, service, or local event codes. Prefer a hospital-wide coded procedure record relation over ICU-only procedure events, device events, medication events, flowsheet events, or other stay-level subsets. Do not combine diagnoses, billing events, or multiple procedure sources. Generate a SELECT filtered only to patient key {patient_key} and all encounter keys in ({encounter_keys}); do not select only one encounter. Preserve every matching procedure row from the selected event relation. Any optional dictionary join MUST be a LEFT JOIN using every column of the documented dictionary composite key so that it cannot remove or multiply event rows; an INNER JOIN or a partial-key join is forbidden. If the complete procedure dictionary join key cannot be proven from metadata, do not join and return NULL AS _display. Return: patient key AS _patient_key, encounter key AS _encounter_key, a non-null unique key built only from that procedure row's documented key columns AS _resource_key, procedure code AS _code, an actual stored canonical URI column AS _code_system otherwise NULL, an actual procedure dictionary description column AS _display otherwise NULL, procedure date/time AS _event_datetime. Do not infer a canonical URI from a code, version, standard name, or table name; return NULL AS _code_system unless the selected source relation stores the URI itself. Prefer a documented event-row primary key or its complete documented composite key. Build a composite key with PostgreSQL CAST(... AS TEXT), ||, and separator literals only; do not hash it or use non-PostgreSQL conversion functions. Never use LIMIT per encounter; apply only the final total limit {limit}. Every expression must use documented columns or NULL; quoted clinical labels and fallback literals are forbidden. Order deterministically and limit {limit}. Fully qualify every relation.

Observation.template: Using only the retrieved PostgreSQL schema metadata, select the broadest hospital-wide laboratory or coded test-result event relation in any of these source schemas: {source_schemas}, plus at most one matching dictionary relation. Prefer a relation with a documented unique event-row identifier, test/item code, event time, value, unit, and reference-range columns over ICU-only chart, flowsheet, device, input, output, or procedure event relations. The selected event relation MUST contain an actual documented test, item, measurement, or observation code column; select that source value AS _code and never return NULL for _code. If a relation has no code column or no stable event-row identifier while a better candidate has one, choose the better relation. Generate a patient-wide SELECT filtered only to patient key {patient_key}; do not restrict observations to encounter, admission, visit, stay, or episode keys. Preserve every matching row from the selected event relation, including rows whose encounter key is NULL. If the selected event relation documents any encounter, admission, visit, stay, or episode key column, you MUST select that source column directly AS _encounter_key; returning a literal NULL for _encounter_key in that case is forbidden. Use NULL only when the event relation truly has no documented encounter-like key. Do not join an encounter relation merely to obtain or validate that key. Any optional dictionary join MUST be a LEFT JOIN that preserves all event rows, and an INNER JOIN is forbidden. Return: patient key AS _patient_key, the documented encounter key AS _encounter_key when stored for that event otherwise NULL, and an event-row identifier AS _resource_key that is non-null and unique across every returned row. When a documented unique event-row identifier or primary key exists, you MUST select only that column AS _resource_key and MUST NOT concatenate other columns. Never include an optional encounter, admission, visit, stay, or episode key in _resource_key because its NULL value would make the resource key NULL. Never use a patient, encounter, visit, or stay key alone as _resource_key; only when no event-row key exists, concatenate enough non-null documented event columns with a single-character '-', ':' or '|' separator to distinguish rows without using a quoted empty-string fallback. Also return the required source observation code AS _code, canonical code-system URI AS _code_system when stored otherwise NULL, source display AS _display, event date/time AS _event_datetime, numeric value AS _value_number, text value AS _value_text, display unit AS _unit, canonical unit-system URI AS _unit_system only when stored otherwise NULL, canonical unit code AS _unit_code only when stored otherwise NULL, reference low AS _reference_low, reference high AS _reference_high, and an actual documented interpretation or result-flag column AS _interpretation otherwise NULL. Do not use a comments, note, or free-text narrative column AS _interpretation. Never invent or normalize unsupported source values. Order deterministically and limit {limit}. Fully qualify every relation.
